policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Wash me thoroughly' renders the word adverbially; the qere imperative הֶרֶב ('multiply [to wash]') and the ketiv infinitive absolute הרבה ('abundantly') both yield 'thoroughly' in English, with no italic supply and no textual note on the verse. The English cannot distinguish the form; base (qere) fallback carries the projection.
